text:
maria: heads-up — running a focused KV cache warmup + eviction replay to reproduce the flakey hit-rate drop we saw on canary.
akhil: nice, which harness are you using? the replay one or synthetic generator?
maria: replay harness with synthetic tail noise. we replayed a 24h production trace but scaled qps to 2k r/s to hit steady-state evictions quickly.
jonathan: important to call out: scaled replay can change inter-arrival distributions. did you preserve original spacing, or use poisson scaling?
maria: we tested both. preserved spacing for one run, poisson for another. the weird hit-rate cliff only shows under poisson scaling.
tara: curious — could be batching heuristics interacting with request bursts. did you lock kernel selection or let runtime auto-pick?
maria: let it auto-pick initially. then did a run with --force-kernel=mkldnn (for CPU-only traces) and another with --force-kernel=cuda-fused. behavior changed.
perf-bot: perf-summary: runA(preserve) hit_rate=0.82 warmup=6m evictions/sec=12
perf-bot: perf-summary: runB(poisson) hit_rate=0.65 warmup=2m evictions/sec=38
akhil: 65% is rough. logs? any evictions targeted to same prefix keys? race on prefix insertion maybe.
maria: pasted a short log excerpt:
```
[2026-03-10T14:03:22Z] KVCache: insert prefix=usr-bio/12345 len=128
[2026-03-10T14:03:22Z] KVCache: evict prefix=usr-bio/98765 reason=LRU
[2026-03-10T14:03:22Z] KVCache: insert prefix=usr-bio/54321 len=128
[2026-03-10T14:03:22Z] KVCache: evict prefix=usr-bio/12345 reason=concurrency-conflict
```
akhil: that "concurrency-conflict" reason is new — where's that code path coming from?
jonathan: looks like lock acquisition failed and we tombstoned entry then evicted. we added that to avoid partial payload corruption under heavy insert contention.
tara: so correctness preserved, but we lose hit-rate. can we change eviction to demote instead of full evict under conflict?
akhil: demote could keep smaller suffixes cached. but we need to ensure memory invariants.
maria: quick experiment: changed conflict policy to "defer-evict" (attempt retry up to 3 times, then demote) — hit-rate bumped to 0.75 under poisson. still not equal to preserved spacing.
jonathan: also check batching windows: under poisson bursts, batcher size spikes, KV lookup path is parallelized per-token and introduces more concurrent cache insertions. knob: batcher.max_window_ms and batcher.concurrent_batches.
tara: can we run a very small apples-to-apples: same QPS, same inter-arrival (poisson), but toggle only the conflict policy? otherwise keep kernel, batching, and seq-len distributions identical.
maria: yes running now. config snippet we used:
```
--replay trace=trace-20260310.json --qps=2000 --pattern=poisson --seed=42 \
--cache.size_mb=512 --cache.conflict_policy=defer-evict --kernels=auto \
--batcher.max_window_ms=8 --batcher.concurrent=4
```
perf-bot: new-run: conflict_policy=defer-evict hit_rate=0.74 warmup=3m evictions/sec=21
perf-bot: baseline-run: conflict_policy=evict-on-conflict hit_rate=0.65 warmup=2m evictions/sec=38
akhil: delta +9pt hit-rate from policy change alone — promising.
jonathan: still worried about kernel selection interplay. can you run the same two conflict policies but force identical kernel (cuda-fused) and identical batcher settings?
maria: queued those jobs. will post results.
tara: don't forget to instrument KV cache per-prefix age histograms and concurrent-insert histogram — helps prove it's contention, not algorithmic bug.
maria: added histograms and a small trace sampler.
(20m later)
maria: results: with cuda-fused and identical batcher: evict-on-conflict hit_rate=0.66, defer-evict hit_rate=0.78. contention peaks at 32 concurrent inserts on hot prefixes.
akhil: so kernel doesn't remove the problem, but defer-evict consistently recovers most hit-rate. good.
jonathan: next: safety review of defer-evict — any chance of unbounded memory growth or live-lock? add a backoff + metric for retry_count.
maria: implemented backoff and max-retries=3. also added a safety eviction budget per-second.
maria: final run with safety knobs: hit_rate=0.77 evictions/sec=15 retry_median=1
tara: looks solid. can we add a short-term canary on dedicated with real traffic and low % rollout? 5% of prod tenants?
akhil: good plan. also update docs explaining why conflict policy exists and tradeoffs (correctness vs hit-rate).
maria: opening PR for runtime change + runbook for ops. tagging you all: @akhil @jonathan @tara :eyes:
jonathan: will review the PR. add a perf regression test in CI replay harness to catch future changes.
maria: already added a replay-case that runs Poisson scaled trace with conflict_policy asserted.
perf-bot: job 4521 completed — regression: none. :party:
